item.description: Many musicians are using their platforms to speak up against the recent murder of Minneapolis resident Renee Nicole Good by ICE. item.title: Washington National Opera Leaving Kennedy Center After 55 Years
item.description: Before the news that the Kennedy Center was being renamed the Trump-Kennedy Center, there was already a slew of protests after Donald Trump appointed himself Kennedy Center chairman, including Ben Folds resigning as National Symphony Orchestra's Artistic Advisor. Now the protests are reaching a fever pitch, and the Washington National Opera is leaving the Kennedy Center where it has performed since the venue opened in 1971. item.title: Jenny Lewis Married Her Dog For Her 50th Birthday
item.description: On Thursday (Jan. 8), Jenny Lewis turned 50. The Rilo Kiley leader celebrated the big birthday by marrying her cockapoo, Bobby Rhubarb, who's immortalized on her 2021 single "Puppy And A Truck." item.title: Bob Weir Dead At 78
item.description: Bob Weir, co-founding singer/guitarist for the Grateful Dead and their various offshoots, has passed away. "He transitioned peacefully, surrounded by loved ones, after courageously beating cancer as only Bobby could," according to a statement posted on his website today that cites "underlying lung issues" as the cause of death. item.title: Lucy Dacus & Chappell Roan Cover The Magnetic Fields At Artists For Aid Benefit
item.description: Last night the third iteration of Mustafa's Artists For Aid benefit concert series went down at Los Angeles' Shrine Ballroom, with proceeds supporting relief efforts in Palestine and Sudan. The event was hosted by Bella Hadid and Pedro Pascal, and featured sets from Clairo (her first performance sing having to drop off November's Camp Flog Gnaw lineup), Geese (their first performance since successfully playing Camp Flog Gnaw), Blood Orange, Alex G, Faye Webster, 070 Shake, Lucy Dacus, and more.

item.title: Excessive Force Reunite For First Show In 30 Years At FYA Fest 2026
item.description: The straight-edge metallic hardcore band Excessive Force were based in Orange County for a few years in the mid-'90s before frontman Dan Gump went on to record with Decontaminate, then leave the scene altogether. At the time of their sole album release, 1995's In Your Blood, Gump (who also ran Life Sentence Records) was an aircraft mechanic in the Marine Corps, which complicated touring plans.
